a2_necessity_set.element: Device state telemetry (on/off events, sensor readings)
a2_necessity_set.justification: Real-time device state data is required to execute automation rules and deliver the core smart home functionality.
The installation address is needed to apply local weather and utility data for energy optimization features.
Detailed home network logs are collected by the router-integration feature but are not required for device automation or product improvement.

a2_necessity_set.justification: App clickstream data is used to identify usability issues and improve the automation rule-creation interface.

a4_benefit_business: Telemetry processing enables NestGrid to identify firmware defects early, reduce support costs, and improve retention through personalized automation features that increase customer satisfaction scores.
a4_benefit_business_fact: Internal data shows a 22% reduction in support tickets for customers using personalized automation recommendations compared to those who do not.
a4_benefit_consumer: Consumers receive responsive, proactive smart home automation that learns their routines, reduces manual configuration effort, and provides energy savings notifications.
a4_benefit_consumer_fact: Customers using adaptive scheduling features reported an average 14% reduction in monthly energy consumption in a 2024 beta cohort study.
a4_benefit_other_stakeholders: Home security monitoring benefits household members beyond the account holder by providing real-time alerts for motion and environmental anomalies.
a4_benefit_other_stakeholders_fact: Household co-residents can receive shared alerts through guest access accounts, extending safety benefits beyond the primary subscriber.
a4_benefit_public: Aggregate anonymized energy telemetry supports utility demand-response programs that reduce peak-load strain on the electrical grid.
a4_benefit_public_fact: NestGrid participates in two utility demand-response programs in California and Texas using opt-in aggregated device data.

a5_harm_pathways.actor: External threat actor or malicious insider with access to cloud storage buckets.
a5_harm_pathways.cause: Misconfigured S3 bucket permissions or compromised API credentials could expose sensitive home presence and security footage data.
a5_harm_pathways.data_involved: Precise home installation address, device event logs, and security camera event clips stored in cloud infrastructure.
a5_harm_pathways.harm: (A) Unauthorized access, destruction, use, modification, or disclosure; loss of availability
a5_harm_pathways.source: Centralized AWS cloud storage containing telemetry data and video clips from consumer homes.

a5_harm_pathways.actor: NestGrid itself through over-broad data collection practices.
a5_harm_pathways.cause: Consumers are not clearly informed that home network traffic beyond device communication is captured, limiting their ability to meaningfully consent or opt out.
a5_harm_pathways.data_involved: Home network traffic logs collected through the router-integration feature beyond what is necessary for automation.
a5_harm_pathways.harm: (C) Impairment of consumer control over personal information
a5_harm_pathways.source: Router-integration SDK that captures full home network logs rather than device-specific traffic.

a5_harm_pathways.actor: Media or regulators following a data breach or privacy complaint.
a5_harm_pathways.cause: A breach or complaint exposing that NestGrid retains home surveillance data beyond consumer expectations could generate significant negative press and erode consumer trust.
a5_harm_pathways.data_involved: Security camera footage and home presence patterns linked to consumer identities.
a5_harm_pathways.source: Public disclosure of a security incident or regulatory investigation involving home surveillance data.

a6_safeguards.safeguard: AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS 1.3 in transit are applied to all telemetry and video clip storage; bucket access is restricted via IAM policies with quarterly access reviews.

a6_safeguards.effectiveness_basis: Based on internal design review only

risk_pathway_ids: (A) Unauthorized access, destruction, use, modification, or disclosure; loss of availability

i1_processing_purpose: NestGrid collects smart home device telemetry—including device state changes, energy usage, motion events, and network activity—to power real-time automation rules, surface personalized recommendations in the mobile app, and identify product defects. A secondary use is sharing anonymized, aggregated usage statistics with analytics partners to benchmark product performance.
i1b_min_pi: Collection is limited to telemetry signals necessary for automation and diagnostics; raw audio and full video frames are processed on-device where possible and only event-triggered clips are transmitted. Home address geolocation is captured once at device setup and not continuously polled.
i2_retention_detail: Telemetry data is purged on a rolling 12-month window; video clips auto-delete after 30 days unless pinned by the user; payment records are retained 7 years for tax and chargeback purposes.
i2_retention_period: Device telemetry: 12 months; event clips: 30 days; account data: duration of relationship plus 3 years; payment records: 7 years.
i4b_sources: Personal information is collected directly from consumers during account registration and device setup, automatically from installed devices and the NestGrid mobile app, and from payment processors at the time of purchase.
i5_admt_human_review: Under the current evaluation design, product managers review model recommendations before any feature is surfaced to consumers; no automated decision affecting consumer rights is issued without human sign-off.
i5_admt_logic: The ML profiling engine under evaluation uses a gradient-boosted classifier trained on historical device event sequences to predict preferred automation schedules and flag anomalous usage patterns; no output directly determines a legally significant outcome.
i6_vendors: AWS (cloud infrastructure and storage), Stripe (payment processing), Mixpanel (product analytics), Zendesk (customer support), and Snowflake (data warehousing).
i7_external_consultees: External privacy counsel at Heller & Morse LLP reviewed data flow diagrams and vendor contracts prior to launch.
i7_internal_contributors: Product Engineering, Data Science, Customer Success, and the Privacy & Legal team contributed to the design of this processing activity.

impact_intake.benefitsRationale: The core automation and energy management benefits are significant and measurable, and risks are addressable through encryption, access controls, and planned data minimization changes to the router-integration SDK.
impact_intake.businessBenefits: Reduced support costs, improved retention, and firmware quality improvements driven by telemetry analysis.
impact_intake.consumerBenefits: Personalized automation, energy savings, and real-time home security alerts.
impact_intake.harmCauses: Cloud misconfigurations, over-broad data collection via router-integration SDK, and potential breach of home surveillance data causing reputational harm.
harmTypes: Unauthorised access, destruction, use, modification, or disclosure
Impairment of consumer control over personal information
impact_intake.safeguards: AES-256 encryption, IAM access controls, incident response plan, and planned SDK contract amendments to limit network traffic collection.
impact_intake.stakeholderBenefits: Shared household members benefit from security alerts via guest access; utilities benefit from demand-response participation.
impact_intake.vulnerable: Consumers with home security cameras and precise geolocation data stored in the cloud, particularly those in shared-housing situations where footage may capture non-account-holder household members.
